(Orlando, Florida) | college = [[Ohio State Buckeyes men's basketball|Ohio State]] (2022–2023) | draft_year = 2023 | draft_round = 1 | draft_pick = 28 | draft_team = [[Utah Jazz]] | career_start = 2023 | years1 = {{nbay|2023|start}}–present | team1 = [[Utah Jazz]] | years2 = [[2023–24 NBA G League season|2023]]–[[2024–25 NBA G League season|2024]] | team2 = →[[Salt Lake City Stars]] | highlights = * Third-team [[List of All-Big Ten Conference men's basketball teams|All-Big Ten]] (2023) * Big Ten All-Freshman Team (2023) * [[Florida Mr. Basketball]] (2022) }} '''Brice Paul Sensabaugh''' ({{IPAc-en|ˈ|s|ɛ|n|s|ə|b|ɔː}} {{respell|SEN|sə|baw}}; born October 30, 2003) is an American professional [[basketball]] player for the [[Utah Jazz]] of the [[National Basketball Association]] (NBA). He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Ohio State Buckeyes men's basketball|Ohio State Buckeyes]]. ==Early life and high school career== Sensabaugh was born in [[Cincinnati|Cincinnati, Ohio]] though he grew up in [[Orlando, Florida]] where he attended [[Lake Highland Preparatory School]].{{Cite web |date=January 15, 2026 |title=Brice Sensabaugh's 21-point first quarter NBA high off bench |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/47616124 |access-date=January 16, 2026 |website=ESPN.com |language=en|agency=ESPN Research and The Associated Press}} He was the team's leading scorer as a sophomore but missed his entire junior season due to a [[meniscus (anatomy)|meniscus]] injury.{{cite web|first=Buddy|last=Collings|title=Brice Sensabaugh back for Lake Highland|url=https://www.orlandosentinel.com/sports/highschool/boys-basketball/os-sp-hs-basketball-private-preview-1123-20211123-w42jxbkitncnbaqpy46iebzmre-story.html|work=[[Orlando Sentinel]]|date=November 23, 2021|access-date=January 18, 2023}}{{cite web|first=Steve|last=Helwagen|title=New Buckeyes: Sensabaugh bounced back from injury to win Mr. Basketball award|url=https://247sports.com/college/ohio-state/LongFormArticle/Ohio-State-Buckeyes-mens-basketball-incoming-freshman-Brice-Sensabaugh-to-contribute-at-forward-spots-188167867/|website=[[247Sports.com]]|date=May 31, 2022|access-date=January 18, 2023}} Sensabaugh averaged 25.1 points, 7.2 rebounds and 1.5 assists per game as a senior and was named [[Florida Mr. Basketball]].{{cite web|first=Buddy|last=Collings|title=Ohio State signee Brice Sensabaugh wins Florida Mr Basketball|url=https://www.orlandosentinel.com/sports/highschool/boys-basketball/os-sp-hs-mr-basketball-0405-20220404-etfbevflufhl3o2jqnw57uxpua-story.html|work=[[Orlando Sentinel]]|date=April 4, 2022|access-date=January 17, 2023}} He was rated a four-star [[college recruiting|recruit]] and committed to playing [[college basketball]] for [[Ohio State Buckeyes men's basketball|Ohio State]] over offers from [[Alabama Crimson Tide men's basketball|Alabama]], [[Georgia Tech Yellow Jackets men's basketball|Georgia Tech]] and [[Florida Gators men's basketball|Florida]].{{cite web|first=Adam|last=Jardy|title=Brice Sensabaugh commits to Ohio State basketball, Chris Holtmann|url=https://www.dispatch.com/story/sports/2021/09/28/ohio-state-buckeyes-basketball-recruiting-orlando-lake-highland-prep-brice-sensabaugh-commits/5893641001/|work=[[The Columbus Dispatch]]|date=September 28, 2021|access-date=January 17, 2023}} After graduating from [[high school]], Sensabaugh played in the [[pro–am]] Kingdom Summer League in [[Ohio]] and scored 51 points in a game.{{cite web|first=Buddy|last=Collings|title=Brice Sensabaugh scores 51; Sean Stewart aids U.S. 17U (4-0)|url=https://www.orlandosentinel.com/sports/highschool/boys-basketball/os-sp-hs-basketball-report-0707-20220706-d6cvn62fyjap5jrkdr7llifw44-story.html|work=[[Orlando Sentinel]]|date=July 6, 2022|access-date=January 18, 2023}} ==College career== Sensabaugh entered his freshman season at Ohio State as a key reserve off the bench.{{cite web |last=Jardy |first=Adam |date=November 18, 2022 |title=Prolific Brice Sensabaugh impressing early for Ohio State basketball |url=https://www.dispatch.com/story/sports/college/basketball/2022/11/18/prolific-brice-sensabaugh-impressing-early-for-ohio-state-basketball/69657372007/ |access-date=January 18, 2023 |work=[[The Columbus Dispatch]]}} Sensabaugh was named the [[Big Ten Conference]] Freshman of the Week for three straight weeks.{{cite web|first=Adam|last=Jardy|title=Brice Sensabaugh's 'ridiculous, God-given touch' leading Ohio State|url=https://www.dispatch.com/story/sports/college/basketball/2023/01/03/brice-sensabaughs-ridiculous-god-given-touch-leading-ohio-state/69770505007/|work=[[The Columbus Dispatch]]|date=January 3, 2023|access-date=January 18, 2023}} He was named third team [[List of All-Big Ten Conference men's basketball teams|All-Big Ten]] and to the Big Ten All-Freshman team at the end of the regular season.{{cite web|first=Adam|last=Jardy|title=Ohio State's Brice Sensabaugh, others earn all-Big Ten honors|url=https://www.dispatch.com/story/sports/college/basketball/2023/03/07/ohio-states-brice-sensabaugh-justice-sueing-all-big-ten-honors/69981237007/|work=[[The Columbus Dispatch]]|date=March 7, 2023|access-date=March 23, 2023}} After the season, Sensabaugh declared for the [[2023 NBA draft]].{{cite web|first=Stephen|last=Means|title=What Brice Sensabaugh declaring for the NBA Draft means for Ohio State basketball|url=https://www.cleveland.com/osu/2023/03/what-brice-sensabaugh-declaring-for-the-nba-draft-means-for-ohio-state-basketball.html|website=[[Cleveland.com]]|date=March 25, 2023|access-date=March 27, 2023}} ==Professional career== The [[Utah Jazz]] selected Sensabaugh with the 28th overall pick in the [[2023 NBA draft]].{{cite web|first=Joe|last=Coles|title=Utah Jazz select Brice Sensabaugh with No. 28 pick of 2023 NBA draft|url=https://www.deseret.com/2023/6/22/23769481/utah-jazz-select-brice-sensabaugh-no-28-pick-of-2023-nba-draft|work=[[Deseret News]]|date=June 22, 2023|access-date=June 23, 2023}} On January 14, 2026, Sensabaugh scored a career-high 43 points, including five three-pointers made, in a 126–128 loss to the [[2025–26 Chicago Bulls season|Chicago Bulls]].{{Cite web |title=Brice Sensabaugh Scores Career-High 43 Points in Utah Jazz Loss to Bulls: Three Takeaways |url=https://utahjazz.com/news/brice-sensabaugh-scores-career-high-43-points-in-utah-jazz-loss-to-bulls-three-takeaways |access-date=January 15, 2026 |website=utahjazz.com |language=en|date=January 14, 2026|last=Spyropoulos|first=Eric}} During this game, Sensabaugh also set the record for most points off the bench in a first quarter, with 21 points. ==Career statistics== {{NBA player statistics
